newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH TV NOVA RESULTS MAY WORSEN AS MKT SHARE DIPS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TV NOVA RESULTS MAY WORSEN AS MKT SHARE DIPS.

text.p: Czech TV Nova, founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder's Central European Media Enterprises Group, on Friday said it could post lower 1996 results due to a drop in its market share.

"We may end this year a bit worse than last year, though we do not have to," Nova Director Vladimir Zelezny told Reuters. "The third quarter was weaker -- the market is such -- and we hope to catch up in the last quarter".
Zelezny said that Nova's market share had eased to 65 in the third quarter, down from nearly 70 percent at the beginning of the year.

"Our challenge is to cope with the situation in which the market for us is stagnating or declining, and simultaneously maintain the station's development, which means a preassure on the internal efficiency."
Zelezny said the strategy for the challenge had been prepared, though he declined to provide its details or Nova's preliminary earnings results.

Nova, launched in 1994 and majority-owned by Central European Media Enterprises Ltd, dipped to 65.0 percent average viewership in the third quarter from 65.4 percent in the second, and 69.9 percent in the first quarter.
"Though expected, the seasonal effect was surprisingly stronger, the summer was cold and sluggish, the Atlanta olympics could have added something to it," Zelezny said.
"But the station's efficiency holds, with the broadcast cashflow margin at 47 percent, which is an excellent efficiency," he added.
Nova was the former East Bloc's first state-wide commercial TV station.

It has captured the lion's share of advertising in the 10 billion crown per year Czech TV market with a steady diet of mostly American-generated action films, soap operas, detective serials, and sitcoms, and sensational news programming.
